newsitem.title: USA: Loewen to respond mid-week to Service Corp. bid.
newsitem.headline: Loewen to respond mid-week to Service Corp. bid.

text.p: Loewen Group Inc., the target of an unsolicited bid by rival Service Corp. International, is expected to respond to the offer by mid-week, a source close to Loewen said Sunday.
The board will hold a meeting in the middle of the week and "they will make a formal announcement with respect to their view of the proposal," said the source who did not want to be identified.

If the board rejects the stock offer, Houston-based Service Corp., North America's top funeral home operator, will likely be forced to sweeten the bid or launch a hostile takeover of its No. 2 rival Loewen.
A spokesman for Loewen declined to comment on a timeframe for the board meeting.

Service Corp. last week made an unsolicited bid valued at $43 per share, or $2.8 billion, for Vancouver, British Columbia-based based Loewen. As part of the offer, Service Corp. would assume about $1.3 billion of Loewen debt.
Service Corp. also has indicated it would be willing to raise the offer if it received access to Loewen's financial data.
The companies have been aggressively building market share through acquisitions of privately-owned facilities.
Just Friday, Loewen announced it was teaming up with merchant bank The Blackstone Group to buy California's Rose Hills Co. and The Rose Hill Memorial Park Association for $240 million.
The source said that Service Corp. also had been interested in buying the assets of Rose Hills. Rose Hills Memorial Park, in the Los Angeles area, is the largest cemetery in North America.
Service Corp. could not be reached for comment.

In an interview Friday, Service Corp. President William Heiligbrodt did not rule out a hostile takeover, saying only that the company was considering all of its options. Analysts have speculated that Service Corp. could pay up to $50 per share for Loewen without earnings dilution.
On Friday, Loewen's stock fell 37.5 cents to $42 on Nasdaq, while Service Corp. dropped 87.5 cents to $30.375.

Loewen has said the Rose Hills acquisition was unrelated to the offer from Service Corp.. In fact, the source said the Loewen board had been meeting to finalise the Rose Hill acquisition when it heard about the Service Corp. offer.

Industry sources have speculated that Service Corp. may face a difficult time winning Loewen if it launches a hostile takeover. Insiders of Loewen, including Chief Executive Raymond Loewen, hold about 20 percent of the company's shares.
